summary:

detailed_description:
Create one uninterrupted full-body cinematic photograph. Turn the marble Diana into a clearly adult living woman with natural skin, subtle pores, dark textured hair following the sculpture's gathered hairstyle, a real layered ivory linen chiton, a leather waist wrap, leather sandals, and a functional leather quiver with wooden arrows. Turn the marble deer into a living fallow deer with tawny fur, alert eyes, natural antlers, and four separate anatomically coherent legs. Translate the sculpture's relationship into a believable living action: Diana and the deer walk calmly together toward the same frame edge; Diana's lowered hand gently rests on the near antler while her other arm reaches toward the quiver. All four deer hooves and both of Diana's feet make independent contact with the forest floor. Move them into a deep green woodland clearing with ferns, moss, tree trunks behind the subjects, filtered sunbeams, atmospheric depth, contact shadows, and matching directional light.

Reconstruct both subjects in three dimensions from a camera moved exactly 90 degrees around the grouping relative to <Picture 1>. The result must be one strict shared side-profile silhouette at human eye height: Diana's nose points directly toward one frame edge, only one eye and one cheek are visible, her shoulders and hips overlap in profile, and the deer's muzzle and torso face the same direction. Do not show either subject frontally or at a three-quarter angle. This is a newly reconstructed camera view, not a rotated flat cutout. Keep the full woman, deer, sandals, four hooves, antlers, and quiver inside the frame. Remove the Louvre interior, stone arches, tiled floor, other sculptures, barrier, pedestal, and every trace of marble. Exactly one clearly adult woman and one deer; no tree stump, plinth, support under or through the deer, rearing pose, floating hoof, extra people or animals, duplicated limbs, fused anatomy, museum objects, text, border, panels, collage, or split screen.
